status: Pilot direction confirmed; architecture, new dependencies and production test changes need approval before implementation.
explicitUserDecisions: Focus remaining review on meaningful UX rather than minor UI fixes.
Build the live version here rather than prepare a developer handoff.
First release: the user's Studio and invited Clients. No open multi-Studio signup in the first pilot.
releaseGoal: An invited Client and Studio Staff can complete a real project journey with shared, durable data and enforced access, using the approved Brisk interface.

uxPriorities.problem: Media actions derive different scopes from the same retained selection.
uxPriorities.evidence: Original audit browser evidence; current source still uses visibleAssets for sharing/download and the full selectedAssetIds for Move/Archive/Delete. No new browser reproduction in this planning turn.
uxPriorities.recommendation: Use one explicit selection scope and disclose hidden selected files before consequential actions. Confirm the chosen policy before implementation.

uxPriorities.problem: Shared read-only Brand Kit logo dialog exposes Replace and Delete.
uxPriorities.evidence: Original audit browser evidence; current LogoDownloadModal still lacks the parent canEdit capability and renders these commands unconditionally. No write bypass claimed or tested.
uxPriorities.recommendation: Make the nested dialog inherit the existing read-only capability, retaining genuine preview/download actions.

uxPriorities.problem: Review-version deletion has no confirmation or recovery step.
uxPriorities.evidence: Original audit evidence; current version control calls deleteReviewVersion directly, which filters out the version. No deletion was performed.
uxPriorities.recommendation: Use the approved ConfirmationDialog with the actual version identity and consequence; retain the last-version safeguard.

scope: Studio versus Client waiting states and timing updates
questions: Is the next action and responsible party clear?
Does the Client know which version and approval they are acting on?
Are Internal and External audiences clear?
Are saved drafts, submitted work and agreed dates distinguished?
Can the user leave or recover without losing work?
finalJourneyReview.boundary: Inspect current UI and existing product decisions first. Do not reopen approved workflows or introduce unapproved redesigns.

currentProductionGaps: Viewer identity and role are simulated in browser state, rather than derived from an authenticated account.
Project and timing updates are stored in browser localStorage; they are not shared durable records across Client and Studio accounts.
File operations, invitations and delivery feedback include prototype-only behaviours. Each pilot-critical consumer needs a real implementation and verified outcome.
Timing warnings use scoped sample assessments; automatic Studio turnaround rules and deadline calculations remain separate unfinished work.

proposedBuildSequence.scope: Sign-in, Studio/Client memberships, project access, shared Client/project records
proposedBuildSequence.acceptance: Invited Client signs in and sees only permitted projects; Staff sees their Studio. Permissions are enforced beyond interface visibility.

proposedBuildSequence.scope: Brief, optional stage flow, team assignment and status handoffs
proposedBuildSequence.acceptance: A real project and submitted Brief remain available across sessions and authorised accounts. Preserve existing assignment/invitation distinctions.

proposedBuildSequence.scope: Private media uploads, versions, comments, review and approval
proposedBuildSequence.acceptance: Real files can be uploaded and accessed by permitted project members, with exact-version approval and protected Internal content. Confirm upload sizes and playback/processing needs before selecting final media infrastructure.

proposedBuildSequence.scope: Project Chat, Updates, timing calculations and final delivery agreement
proposedBuildSequence.acceptance: Actual events and messages are shared in the right audience; deadlines follow approved working-day rules; proposals do not replace agreed dates without Client agreement.

proposedBuildSequence.scope: Private staging rehearsal and invited pilot launch
proposedBuildSequence.acceptance: Complete the journey using separate accounts, verify denied access, durable records, real downloads and backup/recovery procedures. Review the concrete staging result before external rollout.

proposedServices.status: Recommendation only. No services, accounts, subscriptions or dependencies added.
proposedServices.databaseAuthAndPrivateFiles: Supabase candidate: Postgres, passwordless authentication, row-level access policies and private object storage.
proposedServices.hosting: Vercel candidate for the existing Next.js application.
proposedServices.email: Production invitation and sign-in delivery needs a configured transactional email sender; Supabase default SMTP is not sufficient for invited external Clients.
proposedServices.video: Private object storage is not a transcoding decision. Confirm video sizes, formats and review playback requirements before choosing whether a separate video service is needed.
proposedServices.verification: Request approval to add focused automated access-control and data-integrity checks; current repository guidance prohibits tests unless requested.

preservation: No application source, assets, dependencies, mock records or browser state changed in this planning turn.
No production services created, real emails sent, external invitations sent, deployments made, commits or pushes performed.
The existing prototype and approved Brisk UI remain the reference. No branch change or new checkout without Tom's instruction.
